The statement’s tone is constructive on growth and employment but measured on prices: gains are “solid,” unemployment “low,” yet both headline and core inflation remain below 2% with expectations anchored. Consistent with Friedman–Phelps, the Committee refrains from pursuing any short-run inflation–unemployment trade-off, emphasizing a symmetric 2% objective. The commitment to “gradual” adjustments aligns with New Keynesian guidance that expectations-driven Phillips curves (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003) warrant gradualism when inflation is below target. Keeping policy accommodative while signaling further hikes is broadly consistent with rule-like approaches (McCallum and Nelson, 1999; Taylor-style rules), especially with market-based inflation compensation still low. Overall, the communication is modestly positive but deliberately cautious.
